> AI Knows , Where The Waste Goes

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Project Idea & Overview
Many people are unaware of which type of waste should be disposed of in which bin. Improper waste segregation leads to increased pollution, poor recycling efficiency, and environmental hazards. Manual segregation is time-consuming and often inaccurate.
To solve this problem, we developed TrashIQ, an AI-based garbage waste classifier that automatically identifies waste type from an image and suggests the correct bin color.

Waste Categories
Our system classifies waste into four categories:
Wet Waste – Green Bin
Dry Waste – Blue Bin
E-Waste – Red Bin
Hazardous Waste – Yellow Bin

Solution
Users can upload an image of waste, and the model instantly predicts the waste category along with the correct bin color and disposal guidance. This helps improve waste segregation at the source, reduces human error, and promotes recycling.

The model was trained using a Kaggle waste dataset, and the project logo was designed using Canva

**Challenges we ran into**

First-time Project Experience 
This was our very first complete project, so we faced several initial challenges in understanding the overall workflow, project structure, and how different components (frontend, backend, and model) interact with each other. Despite this, we consistently experimented, learned, and improved step by step.

Backend Compatibility Issues (TensorFlow & Python Versions)
One major hurdle was the compatibility mismatch between TensorFlow and Python versions. Certain TensorFlow versions did not support newer Python releases, which caused repeated build and runtime errors. We resolved this by researching official documentation and aligning the Python version with a compatible TensorFlow release.

Deployment Challenges
Deployment was another significant challenge. We attempted to deploy the project on Render, Railway, and Hugging Face Spaces. Each platform had its own constraints related to runtime environments, dependency installation, and system requirements, which led to multiple failures during the process. Through trial, error, and careful debugging of logs, we gained a better understanding of deployment workflows and platform limitations.

Learning Through Persistence  
Although the journey involved frequent errors and setbacks, each issue helped us strengthen our problem-solving skills. With continuous debugging, documentation reading, and experimentation, we managed to overcome these challenges and successfully run the project locally.

Overall, these challenges played a crucial role in improving our technical understanding and confidence in handling real-world development issues.

**AI**

Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning (AI/ML)
Our project uses machine learning and image classification to identify different types of garbage from uploaded images and predict the correct waste category and bin color.

Sustainability & Environment
The solution helps in proper waste segregation, reduces pollution, and promotes recycling and eco-friendly waste management.

Smart Cities
This project can support smart city initiatives by improving waste management systems through automation and technology.

Social Impact
The system spreads awareness about correct waste disposal and encourages people to follow proper waste segregation practices

### MindGuardAI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mindguardai-8be8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AlvinoShatto/MindGuardAI.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/6w7pLIq3O7c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Code%20Kalari-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://code-kalari.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Detecting distress before it becomes a crisis

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Mental health challenges among students have become a growing concern in educational institutions worldwide. Academic pressure, social expectations, personal struggles, and uncertainty about the future often contribute to stress, anxiety, depression, and emotional exhaustion. Despite the increasing prevalence of these issues, a large number of students suffer in silence, either due to stigma surrounding mental health or lack of accessible support systems. As a result, early warning signs of psychological distress frequently go unnoticed until they escalate into serious or life-threatening conditions.

Traditional mental health support mechanisms rely heavily on students seeking help or on periodic counseling sessions. However, these methods are insufficient for continuous monitoring of emotional well-being. Counselors and mental health professionals cannot realistically track the daily mental state of every student, especially in large institutions. This gap leads to delayed identification of high-risk individuals, missed opportunities for early intervention, and, in extreme cases, tragic outcomes such as self-harm or suicide.

Another critical challenge is the absence of scalable and objective tools to analyze emotional expressions. Students may express distress subtly through language rather than explicit statements. Manual observation or self-reporting often fails to capture these nuances, making it difficult to assess risk accurately and consistently across a large population.

MindGuard AI addresses these challenges by introducing an AI-driven mental health monitoring system designed for early detection and timely support. The platform allows students to perform daily emotional check-ins in a safe, private, and non-judgmental environment. Using natural language processing and sentiment analysis, MindGuard AI evaluates students’ responses and classifies their mental health risk levels as low, medium, or high. In addition, it incorporates keyword-based overrides to immediately identify expressions of severe distress or suicidal intent.

By automating the risk assessment process, MindGuard AI enables institutions to monitor student well-being at scale without overburdening human counselors. High-risk cases are promptly flagged for administrative or professional attention, allowing timely human intervention while maintaining student privacy and dignity. Importantly, the system does not replace mental health professionals but acts as an intelligent support tool that enhances existing care frameworks.

In conclusion, MindGuard AI solves the critical problem of delayed and insufficient mental health monitoring in educational environments. By combining artificial intelligence with empathetic design, it bridges the gap between students in distress and the support they need, ensuring that no warning sign goes unnoticed and that help reaches students before a crisis occurs.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges in developing MindGuard AI was implementing session-based authentication across different origins. Managing cookies, CORS configuration, and maintaining login state without using JWT required careful debugging to ensure users remained authenticated after page refreshes.

Another challenge was integrating the AI sentiment analysis model, which initially caused memory-related crashes when loaded at application startup. This issue was resolved by implementing lazy loading, improving system stability and performance.

Designing accurate risk classification logic was also challenging. Sentiment analysis alone was not sufficient, so a keyword-based override mechanism was added to ensure high-risk cases were detected reliably.

Overall, these challenges involved balancing technical complexity, system performance, and ethical responsibility, making the development process both demanding and educational.

### TribalEarth 360
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tribalearth-aipowered-fra-atlas-and-webgis-dss-760b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/DharunNagavel/Tribal-Earth-360.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tribal-earth-360.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20Space%202025-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-space-1.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Where AI Meets Forest Rights Governance

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Support Vector Machine (SVM)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support%20Vector%20Machine%20(SVM)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Convolutional neural network (CNN)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Convolutional%20neural%20network%20(CNN)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Long short-term memory (LSTM)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Long%20short--term%20memory%20(LSTM)-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

#### Problem Statement  
The implementation of the **Forest Rights Act (FRA)** in India faces persistent challenges due to **fragmented, paper-based records, lack of spatial visibility, and absence of real-time monitoring mechanisms**. FRA data is often stored in physical files or isolated departmental databases, making verification slow and error-prone. Government officials struggle to accurately identify FRA land boundaries, track land-use changes, detect encroachments, or assess whether eligible patta holders are receiving appropriate welfare schemes. This results in **delayed decision-making, land disputes, poor inter-departmental coordination, and limited transparency**, ultimately weakening the intended social and environmental impact of the Act.

#### Solution: TribalEarth 360  
**TribalEarth 360** addresses these issues by delivering an **AI-powered, WebGIS-based FRA Atlas and Decision Support System (DSS)** designed specifically for government use. The platform digitizes legacy FRA records using **OCR and NLP**, converting unstructured and handwritten documents into standardized digital assets. It integrates **satellite imagery and AI models (CNN, U-Net, NDVI)** to generate accurate spatial maps of FRA lands, including forests, agricultural plots, water bodies, and homesteads. These datasets are visualized through an interactive WebGIS interface, enabling officials to monitor land usage, detect changes, and verify claims in near real time.

The built-in **Decision Support System** further enhances governance by analyzing FRA patta data alongside socio-economic indicators to **automatically generate scheme eligibility recommendations** for beneficiaries. Secure role-based access ensures that sensitive land and personal data are protected, while automated reports and alerts help policymakers respond quickly to emerging issues.

#### What Makes It Unique  
What sets **TribalEarth 360** apart is its **end-to-end, AI-driven approach** tailored exclusively to FRA governance. Unlike conventional GIS portals that only display maps, TribalEarth 360 **generates new digital records, spatial intelligence, and policy insights** from raw documents and satellite data. It unifies **record digitization, geospatial monitoring, and decision support** into a single platform, eliminating data silos across departments. The system is designed specifically for **FRA-designated lands**, not generic land management, ensuring higher relevance and accuracy. Its ability to provide **real-time, AI-generated insights and scheme recommendations** makes it a powerful governance tool that enhances transparency, reduces disputes, and strengthens the overall implementation of the Forest Rights Act.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Low-quality and inconsistent FRA records**  
   Many Forest Rights Act (FRA) documents were handwritten, faded, or scanned poorly, leading to inaccurate OCR results.  
   **How I overcame it:** I implemented image preprocessing (noise removal, contrast enhancement, skew correction) and combined OCR with NLP-based text cleaning and field validation to generate reliable structured records.

2. **Incorrect land-use classification from satellite images**  
   Seasonal changes, dense forest cover, and cloud interference caused misclassification of forest, farmland, and water bodies.  
   **How I overcame it:** I used NDVI-based vegetation indices along with U-Net and CNN models trained on multi-temporal satellite data to improve segmentation accuracy.

3. **Slow performance in WebGIS visualization**  
   Rendering large geospatial datasets and multiple layers caused lag and browser crashes.  
   **How I overcame it:** I optimized performance using server-side map tiling, PostGIS spatial indexing, and lazy loading of GIS layers.

4. **Integrating outputs from multiple AI models**  
   Different AI modules produced data in varying formats, making integration into the DSS difficult.  
   **How I overcame it:** I designed a unified data schema and a microservice-based backend to standardize outputs before feeding them into the Decision Support System.

5. **Ensuring data security and access control for government users**  
   Sensitive land and beneficiary data required strict access management.  
   **How I overcame it:** I implemented JWT-based authentication with role-based access control (RBAC) to ensure only authorized government officials could access specific data and features.

**Generative AI**

TribalEarth 360 comes under the Generative AI track because it goes beyond simple data classification or rule-based automation and actively creates new, usable intelligence from raw and unstructured inputs. The system uses OCR and NLP to transform handwritten and scanned Forest Rights Act (FRA) records into clean, standardized digital records, effectively generating structured data that did not exist in machine-readable form earlier. This process involves AI-driven understanding, correction, and normalization of historical documents.

In addition, the platform applies AI models such as CNN, U-Net, and NDVI-based analysis on satellite imagery to generate spatial layers and land-use maps identifying forests, agricultural land, water bodies, and homesteads. These maps are not pre-available datasets but are AI-generated geospatial assets derived from raw satellite pixels. Furthermore, the Decision Support System (DSS) analyzes FRA patta data, socio-economic indicators, and land characteristics to generate dynamic scheme recommendations and policy insights for government authorities.

By also producing automated reports, alerts, and real-time insights for policymakers and continuously improving its outputs as new data arrives, TribalEarth 360 demonstrates core Generative AI capabilities. Hence, it fits the Generative AI track as it converts unstructured records and imagery into newly generated digital assets, spatial intelligence, and decision-ready outputs, enabling smarter governance of forest rights.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Urban planners, researchers, and sustainability teams currently lack a simple way to understand where carbon emissions are highest and which interventions will create the most impact before investing.

Decisions are often made using:

*City-level averages

*Static reports

*Trial-and-error implementation

This leads to inefficient spending, delayed action, and uncertain climate and health outcomes.

How People Can Use It

*Our platform enables users to:

*Identify high-emission urban blocks and buildings

*Understand how traffic, land use, density, and green cover influence emissions

*Compare multiple carbon reduction interventions before deployment

*Estimate CO₂ reduction, carbon credits, and cost in advance

*Visualize before-and-after impact using maps and graphs

*Generate ready-to-use reports for planning and decision-making

How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier & Safer

*Reduces trial-and-error urban investments

*Helps planners choose the most cost-effective solution

*Enables data-driven climate decisions, not assumptions

*Supports health-aware planning by linking emissions to air quality and respiratory risk

*Makes sustainability planning faster, localized, and actionable

**Challenges we ran into**

1. No single API gives direct CO₂ data at block level

At the beginning, we assumed there might be an API that directly provides CO₂ emissions for any location. We quickly realized that accurate CO₂ data at a building or block level is not publicly available and requires physical sensors.

How we solved it:
We shifted our approach to a relative CO₂ intensity model, using scientifically accepted proxies such as traffic congestion, air-quality indicators, building density, and green cover. This made the model realistic, explainable, and suitable for urban planning.

2. Integrating multiple real-time data sources

Combining traffic data, air quality data, and OpenStreetMap urban data into a single workflow was challenging due to different data formats, rate limits, and response times.

How we solved it:
We designed a modular data pipeline, where each data source is processed independently and normalized before being combined into the CO₂ intensity score. We also added fallback logic when an API is unavailable.

3. Handling API limitations and reliability

Free-tier APIs have rate limits and occasional failures, which affected real-time testing during development.

How we solved it:
We implemented graceful fallbacks using rule-based assumptions and cached recent results to ensure the application always responds smoothly during demos.

4. Balancing accuracy with simplicity

There was a constant trade-off between building a very complex scientific model and keeping the system simple, fast, and explainable for judges and users.

How we solved it:
We intentionally avoided black-box machine learning and instead focused on transparent, interpretable logic that clearly shows how each factor contributes to the final output.

5. Visualizing complex data in an intuitive way

Displaying multiple parameters like CO₂ intensity, traffic, AQI, and intervention impact on a 3D map without overwhelming users was difficult.

How we solved it:
We used progressive disclosure — showing high-level insights first and allowing users to drill down only when needed. This kept the interface clean while still being powerful.

**InsForge**

Our project uses Inforge as the backend data layer to manage, store, and process the multiple urban datasets required for CO₂ intensity simulation.

Instead of directly computing results from live APIs every time a user interacts with the map, we use Inforge to store structured data fetched from external APIs such as traffic, air quality, land-use, and green cover data.

Why We Used Inforge?

Urban sustainability analysis requires combining multiple data sources that differ in format, frequency, and reliability. Inforge allows us to:

Persist API responses in a centralized database

Reduce repeated API calls and rate-limit issues

Enable faster, more reliable simulations

Maintain historical snapshots for comparison and research

How the Data Flow Works?

User selects a city or block on the 3D map

Backend fetches real-time data from:

Traffic APIs

Air quality APIs

OpenStreetMap-based urban datasets

These datasets are stored and normalized in the Inforge database

Our CO₂ intensity calculation engine runs on the stored data

Results are returned instantly to the frontend for visualization

Role of Inforge in CO₂ Intensity Calculation

Inforge acts as the single source of truth for our simulation engine.
All CO₂ intensity calculations are performed using data retrieved from Inforge, ensuring:

Consistency across simulations

Reproducibility of results

Faster “what-if” intervention comparisons

Scalability to multiple cities and users

**Gemini API**

# 🤖 Gemini AI Integration

This project uses **Google Gemini 2.5 Flash** to act as an **Urban Environmental Consultant**, providing real-time, context-aware analysis of simulation results.

---

## 1. Architecture

The AI layer is implemented in the backend (`server.js`) to secure API keys and handle data processing before querying the model.

- **Model Used:** `gemini-2.5-flash`  
  *(Chosen for high rate limits and low latency)*

- **Data Inputs:**  
  The AI receives a rich context payload including:
  - **Coordinates:** Precise location (Lat/Lon)
  - **Urban Morphology:** Building density, tree density, and area type (e.g., *High Density Urban*)
  - **Traffic Patterns:** 30-day historical traffic speed trends
  - **Air Quality History:** 30-day AQI trends (batched into weekly summaries)
  - **Intervention Data:** Type of technology applied (e.g., *Green Wall*) and its immediate physics-based impact

---

## 2. Prompt Engineering

We use a structured prompt to force the AI into a specific role and output format, ensuring the frontend always receives parseable JSON.

```javascript
const prompt = `
  Role: Urban Environmental Consultant.
  Response Format: JSON ONLY.
  
  Context:
  - Location: ${lat}, ${lon} (${buildingDensity}, ${treeDensity} trees).
  - Intervention: ${intervention} (Targeting AQI ${newAQI}).
  
  **Weekly Analysis (Past Month):**
  - AQI Trend: ${JSON.stringify(weeklyAQI)}
  - Traffic Trend: ${JSON.stringify(weeklyTraffic)}
  
  Task:
  1. Analyze the 4-week trend (e.g. "AQI spiked in Week 2").
  2. Suggest a "Pro" tech version of ${intervention}.
  3. Predict next 7 days (Forecast).

  Output JSON:
  {
    "headline": "5-word punchy title",
    "content": "Analysis of the weekly trend and why this tech fits.",
    "tech_specs": "Specific tech name (e.g. 'IoT Active Moss')",
    "recommendation": "Strategic advice based on the weekly data.",
    "aqi": [7 numbers],
    "traffic": [7 numbers]
  }
`;

## 3. Fail-Safe Mechanisms

To ensure the dashboard never breaks during high traffic or API outages, a robust fallback system is implemented:

- **Rate Limit Handling:**  
  If Gemini returns a `429 Too Many Requests` error, the server catches it immediately.

- **Local Fallback Generator:**  
  A procedural function `generateFallbackInsight()` creates a professional-sounding response and standard mathematical forecasts.

- **Token Optimization:**  
  Historical data is batched into **4 weekly averages** before sending to Gemini, reducing input token usage by ~80% and speeding up response times.

---

## 4. Output Visualization

The JSON output from Gemini is rendered in the `AnalyticsView` component:

- **Forecast Graphs:**  
  The `aqi` and `traffic` arrays are plotted alongside real historical data.

- **Insight Card:**  
  The `headline`, `tech_specs`, and `recommendation` are displayed in a dedicated strategy card.

**The problem it solves**

In India, where annual waste generation exceeds 62 million tonnes, the integrity of the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework is threatened by "digital replay attacks"—a fraud method where users photograph screens displaying waste rather than physical objects to illegally claim recycling credits. With verified digital fraud cases in India rising by over 50% year-on-year, current manual auditing cannot keep pace with this sophistication. Our problem statement addresses this critical trust gap by automating the detection of "screen recapture" artifacts (like Moiré patterns) and duplicate submissions, ensuring that every allocated EPR credit corresponds to verified, ground-truth physical recycling activity.

**Challenges we ran into**

Technical:
  Circular imports: Fixed with lazy imports and dependency injection
  Android threading: Network calls on main thread crashes, used Retrofit's enqueue()

Integration:
  JSON mismatches: Aligned Kotlin data classes with Flask response structure
  Network config: Flask on 0.0.0.0 with firewall adjustments

Accuracy:
  False positives: Two-stage moiré detection with Laplacian filter first
  Threshold tuning: Adjusted Hamming distance for better fraud detection

Process:
   Debugging: Added logging interceptors and incremental testing
   Time constraints: Prioritized core features (upload, dHash, moiré)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Cities commonly struggle with unequal water distribution, inconsistent supply timings, undetected leakages, slow complaint handling, and a lack of transparency for citizens. Municipal teams often work with disconnected systems and limited real-time data, leading to supply imbalance, operational inefficiency, and citizen dissatisfaction.

The Fair Water Distribution Management System (FWDMS) solves these issues by centralizing monitoring, automation, analytics, and transparency into a single system.

How It Solves the Problem (Municipal Perspective)

Municipal operators get a unified system that provides:

**Live Network Pressure Monitoring**

Shows real-time pressure across zones, enabling immediate detection of issues such as leaks or supply drops.

**AI-Based Demand Forecasting**

Predicts water demand patterns and peak hours to enable better planning and fair distribution.

**Pump Schedule Optimization**

Improves pump usage efficiency, reduces energy waste, and strengthens supply reliability.

**Energy Consumption Insights**

Displays pump-wise energy usage data to help control operational costs.

**Interactive Zone Map
**
Visual representation of pipelines, pumps, and pressure values to improve decision-making.

**Billing and Automatic Invoice Generation**

Automates the billing process, reduces manual errors, and ensures transparency.

**Leakage and Water Theft Detection**

Identifies sudden pressure drops and alerts the municipality to potential theft or pipe damage.

**Citizen Reward Mechanism
**
Encourages citizens to report leaks and low-pressure issues by offering reward points.

**Emergency Service Contacts**

Provides immediate access to critical support teams for urgent water-related issues.

How It Helps Citizens

The citizen portal is designed to improve accessibility, transparency, and trust:

**Billing, History, and Supply Status**

Displays the user’s current bill, payment history, due dates, and supply status (Active, Limited, or Suspended).
**
Fairness Index and Supply Insights**

Shows how fair the water distribution is in their area, along with interruptions, peak usage times, and complaint resolution rates.

**Reward Points**

Citizens can earn and redeem points for reporting leaks, low pressure, or other issues.

**Real-Time Alerts and Schedules
**
Keeps users informed about supply timings, changes, low-pressure warnings, and maintenance schedules.

**Issue Reporting System**

Allows citizens to report leaks, theft, or low pressure with details and attachments for faster municipal action.

Summary

The Fair Water Distribution Management System makes water distribution:

Fair for citizens

Efficient for municipal authorities

Transparent for everyone

**Challenges we ran into**

Building the Fair Water Distribution Management System (FWDMS) came with several technical and architectural challenges. Each hurdle pushed us to refine our design decisions and improve the overall system.

1. Integrating Multiple Data Streams

We had to combine pressure readings, pump data, demand forecasts, billing details, and citizen inputs into a single platform.
The challenge was maintaining consistency and preventing UI lag.
How we solved it:
We adopted React Query for caching and FastAPI’s async endpoints to ensure smooth data flow and real-time updates.

2. Real-Time Pressure and Telemetry

Streaming live pressure updates caused synchronization and performance issues during testing.
Solution:
We implemented a WebSocket-based telemetry stream and optimized the backend for async event handling.

3. Detecting Leakage & Water Theft

Simulating sudden pressure drops and mapping them to alerts required accurate conditional logic and threshold tuning.
Solution:
We added configurable pressure thresholds, simple anomaly detection logic, and clear alert rules.

4. GIS / Interactive Zone Map Integration

Displaying ward-wise data with markers, colors, and tooltips in Leaflet was challenging due to coordinate mismatches and re-render issues.
Solution:
We normalized zone boundaries, built reusable map components, and introduced debounced updates for better performance.

5. Billing System & Invoice Generation

Generating bills and auto-invoices while syncing payment status between citizen and municipal panels was initially inconsistent.
Solution:
We refactored the billing schema, used unique identifiers for each invoice, and added backend validation.

6. Authentication Flow Changes

We initially planned OTP login but later shifted to email–password authentication.
Solution:
We modified the auth router, added hashing, validation schemas, and integrated JWT-based secure sessions.

7. Reward System Logic

Ensuring fair points for citizens without abuse (e.g., spam reports) was tricky.
Solution:
We added rate-limiting, verification checks, and reward rules tied to incident resolution.

8. Coordination Within the Team

With responsibilities split across frontend, backend, and ML forecasting, ensuring alignment was sometimes difficult.
Solution:
We used shared API docs, GitHub coordination, and feature-wise task ownership to streamline collaboration.

**The problem it solves**

This system moves Raipur's water management from a reactive, "guesswork" model to a proactive, "data-driven" model. It makes existing tasks easier, safer, and more efficient for everyone involved.

# 1. For Municipal Authorities & Control Room Operators
This group moves from being "problem responders" to "network managers."

From Guesswork to Insight:

Before: Relying on angry phone calls and "gut feelings" to know where problems are.

After: They use your HMI (dashboard) to get a single, real-time view of the entire city's pressure and flow. They can see a problem before the first phone call.

From Blunt Instruments to Surgical Control:

Before: Using city-wide "power cuts" to manage over-pumping—an inefficient, unfair, and "blunt" tool.

After: They use your AI-driven recommendations and VFD controls to make surgical adjustments. They can approve a fix like "increase Pump 5 to 80%" to solve a shortage in Zone 7, which is easier, faster, and fairer for all citizens.

From Chaos to Efficiency:

Before: Juggling phone calls, paper reports, and radio chatter to manage leaks.

After: Your Alarm Server and Citizen Portal centralize all alerts—both AI-detected leaks and citizen reports—onto one map, allowing them to dispatch field crews with precision.

# 2. For Field & Maintenance Workers
This group moves from being "observers" to "first responders."

From Wasted Time to Precise Action:

Before: Driving to a general "Zone 7" to "look for a reported leak" based on a vague phone call.

After: They receive a dispatch with a geolocation tag from the citizen report or a specific pipe segment from the AI's "Unaccounted-for-Water" calculation. They go directly to the problem, saving hours of time and fuel.

From Reactive to Proactive Repairs:

Before: Only being called when a pipe bursts, which is a dangerous, high-pressure emergency.

After: The system's AI-driven anomaly detection (e.g., "pressure spike detected in Zone 3") can alert them to a potential burst before it happens, making the task significantly safer.

# 3. For Citizens (Especially "Tail-End" Households)
This is the group that benefits the most, moving from "victims" of the system to "stakeholders."

From Inequity to Fairness:

Before: Experiencing daily water shortages because over-pumping in other zones prevents water from reaching them.

After: The system's primary goal is to maintain pressure for them. The Pressure Transducers in their zones act as their digital advocate, ensuring the AI and admins must balance the network to serve them.

From Helplessness to Empowerment:

Before: Calling a city hotline and hoping someone eventually does something about their report.

After: Submitting a report via the Citizen Portal creates a trackable, geolocated ticket. They are no longer just complaining; they are actively participating in the city's maintenance workflow.

From Unreliability to Predictability:

Before: Unannounced water shortages and city-wide power cuts that disrupt their lives.

After: The system creates a stable, balanced network. This provides a reliable and predictable supply of water, allowing them to cook, clean, and live without uncertainty.

# 4. For City Planners & Leadership
This group moves from "political budgeting" to "data-driven investment."

From Guesswork to Data-Driven Planning:

Before: Deciding where to build new infrastructure based on which neighborhood complains the loudest.

After: They use your Historian (database), which contains years of real-world data, to make billion-rupee decisions. They can prove which pipes are failing, which zones are growing, and where the next pump station is truly needed.

From Wasted Money to Cost Savings:

Easier Cost Reduction: The AI automatically saves money by running pumps during cheap, off-peak electricity hours.

Easier Asset Management: Leak detection saves millions of liters of treated water—a direct cost saving.

Smarter Budgets: They can track KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) like "Mean Time to Repair" and "Unaccounted-for-Water," proving to the public that services are improving.

**Challenges we ran into**

## The Challenge: The "Lagging HMI" and UI Flicker
The most significant hurdle we ran into was UI performance related to high-frequency data.

Our HMI (dashboard) is designed to be a "live" system. Our backend service (whether a simulation or a real RTU feed) pushes new pressure and flow data for all 10 zones every few seconds.

## The Specific Bug: The "Waterfall Re-render"
Our first version had a critical bug: when data for just one zone (e.g., Zone 3) was updated, our entire dashboard would flicker and re-render.

The "Live Zone Stats" cards for all 10 zones would blink.

The Recharts chart would lag or reset its animation.

The Leaflet map would stutter.

This made the HMI unusable for an operator who needs to see stable, at-a-glance data.

## The Root Cause
The problem wasn't the database or the network—it was our React state management.

We had made a common mistake: we stored all live zone data in a single, top-level state object (e.g., const [zones, setZones] = useState(...)).

When our setZones function was called to update Zone 3's pressure, React saw the entire zones object as "new." It then told every single component that depended on that object (all 10 stat cards, the chart, the map) to re-render themselves, even though their own data hadn't changed.

## How We Solved It
We solved this with a two-part approach focused on decoupling state and memoization.

Using React.memo for Component Memoization:

We wrapped our individual "Live Zone Stats" card component in React.memo.

This is a "higher-order component" that tells React: "Do not re-render this component unless its own props have actually changed."

This immediately stopped the 9 other cards from re-rendering, as their props (e.g., zoneName, pressure) remained identical.

Optimizing the Data Flow (Supabase Realtime):

Instead of constantly fetching all data, we implemented Supabase Realtime.

Our dashboard now subscribes to changes on the zone_history table.

When the backend updates a row, Supabase pushes only that single, new piece of data to the HMI.

This was far more efficient than polling and ensured our component state was only updated with actual changes

**Web2.0 Track**

1. User-Generated Content (UGC)
Web 1.0: The city posts a static "Water Schedule" PDF. Citizens are passive consumers of information.

Your Web 2.0 Project: The Citizen Feedback Portal transforms citizens into active participants and data creators. They generate valuable, geolocated content (leak reports, shortage alerts, photos) that is fed directly into the system. This UGC is treated as a first-class data source, equal in importance to the mechanical sensors.

2. The Web as a Platform (Rich Internet Applications)
Web 1.0: A static HTML page with a "Submit" button that requires a full-page reload.

Your Web 2.0 Project: Your Admin HMI is a true Rich Internet Application (RIA).

It runs entirely in the browser.

It uses asynchronous data feeds (from your simulation/Supabase) to update the Leaflet map and Recharts in real-time without a page reload.

This dynamic, responsive, single-page-app (SPA) experience is the very definition of the web as a platform, not just a document viewer.

3. Social Feedback & Community
Web 1.0: A "contact_us@city.gov" email address that goes into a black hole.

Your Web 2.0 Project: You create a social feedback loop.

A citizen submits a report (UGC).

It appears instantly on the admin's HMI.

The admin can dispatch a crew and (in a future step) mark the issue as "Resolved," which could notify the citizen.

This builds a transparent, two-way communication channel between the users (citizens) and the providers (city), fostering a community around a shared resource.

4. Data "Mashups"
Web 1.0: A self-contained, isolated website.

Your Web 2.0 Project: Your application is a "mashup" that intelligently combines multiple data sources to create new value.

Source 1: Your sensor data (from the simulation).

Source 2: Your user-generated content (from citizens).

Source 3: External map tiles (from Leaflet/OpenStreetMap).

You are mashing up these different data streams into a single, cohesive, and intelligent application.

**Challenges we ran into**

We planned to deploy and integrate our backend application using API Gateway and AWS Lambda services. However, we encountered an issue when uploading the ZIP file to create the Lambda function. Initially, it did not support Linux. To address this, I used the Cloud Shell, uploaded my app.py and requirements.txt files to the Cloud Shell IDE, downloaded the repo.zip file, and then uploaded it to create the Lambda function. This worked fine with API Gateway, but we faced several issues with the Lambda function itself. Some required modules were not installed, leading to multiple errors when integrating API Gateway with Lambda functions. Due to these difficulties, we ultimately decided to deploy the backend on Vercel instead.

### Green Reaction predictor
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/green-reaction-predictor-f68b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MayuriTirole/AI_Green_Reaction_Optimizer.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20On%20Hills%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackonhills7.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI Green Reaction Optimizer — revolutionizing chem

![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Anaconda](https://img.shields.io/badge/Anaconda-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Plotly](https://img.shields.io/badge/Plotly-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The AI Green Reaction Optimizer is an intelligent tool designed to assist chemists, researchers, and students in optimizing chemical reactions efficiently and sustainably. By simply entering parameters such as temperature, catalyst concentration, and solvent structure (via SMILES code), users can instantly predict the expected reaction yield through an interactive dashboard. This eliminates the need for repeated trial-and-error experiments, allowing users to explore different reaction conditions digitally before performing them in the lab.

The platform makes the process of reaction optimization significantly easier, safer, and faster. It simplifies complex chemical data analysis and provides visual insights into how changes in temperature, catalysts, and solvents affect reaction efficiency. By reducing the number of physical experiments, it ensures safer laboratory practices, minimizing exposure to hazardous chemicals and preventing waste from failed reactions. Moreover, it drastically accelerates research by using machine learning to simulate thousands of reaction possibilities within minutes, helping scientists identify optimal conditions for maximum yield and minimal environmental impact.

In essence, the AI Green Reaction Optimizer acts as a digital chemist, offering data-driven predictions that save time, reduce costs, and promote eco-friendly, high-yield chemical processes—paving the way for a more sustainable and efficient future in chemical research and industrial applications.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge faced during the development of the AI Green Reaction Optimizer was a data mismatch issue between the model and the scaler used during prediction. Initially, the model was trained on one version of the dataset while the prediction script used another, leading to a feature count mismatch and errors such as “ValueError: X has 2050 features, but StandardScaler is expecting 130 features as input.” This issue occurred because the preprocessing steps and the number of molecular fingerprint bits were not consistent across the different scripts. To overcome this, we standardized the entire data pipeline to ensure that both the training and prediction stages used the same preprocessing logic. We also ensured that the same scaler file (scaler.pkl) used during training was saved and reloaded during prediction for consistent feature scaling. Additionally, we introduced debugging print statements and shape checks to validate the number of features throughout the workflow. After these fixes, the model and preprocessing became fully synchronized, leading to stable and realistic yield predictions. This experience highlighted the importance of maintaining a unified and reproducible data processing pipeline in machine learning projects, particularly in scientific applications where precision and consistency are critical.

Team **PromptRunners** -- Khushboo Sharma, [Tirth Marakana](https://github.com/gujjutirth), Mayuri Tirole, [Kshitij Chauhan](https://github.com/KN-lang)

**The problem it solves**

Stablecoins are growing. However, managing and investing them onchain still feels like work.

Users switch between wallets, networks, and dashboards just to check balances, send funds, or find a safe place to earn yield.

The result: fragmented accounts, wasted time, and missed opportunities.

BANB changes this by bringing the **simplicity of a neobank to the onchain world powered by AI.**

With BANB, users can:

- Connect multiple wallets and manage all their stablecoins from one place — no more chain switching.

- Ask simple questions like “Where should I move my USDC?” and get AI-guided insights that explain yield, risk, and timing.

- Act instantly from any connected wallet, keeping full self-custody and onchain control.

- Save time and reduce friction — BANB turns complex DeFi actions into one clear command or click.

In short: BANB gives you the UX of a neobank with the control of Web3, helping users manage and grow their stablecoins effortlessly.

BANB doesn’t just show your crypto. It helps you use it, safely and intelligently.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building BANB requires connecting traditional UX patterns with blockchain-native systems without sacrificing decentralization.

Some of the key hurdles included:

- Instant on/off ramp without KYC:
Bridging fiat methods (Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal) with on-chain USDC flow was difficult due to API inconsistencies and compliance restrictions.

- Investment P&L tracking (e.g., Morpho vaults):
On-chain data is fragmented across protocols.
→ We are looking into DeFi APIs like Lambda to track this.

- Non-custodial revenue layer:
Designing yield and operational fees without custody required balancing smart contract logic and transparent transaction recording.
→ Solved by adding fees on top of 3rd party service providers (on/off ramp) and by creating intermediary smart contracts acting as the investment owner but controlled by the user. Not implemented yet.

- AI Agent integration:
Bridging wallet actions with natural language input through LLMs involved designing intent-to-transaction mapping.
→ Created a middleware layer connecting LLM → Agent → Transaction Crafting module. Not implemented yet.

**Link to the GitHub Repo of your project**

https://github.com/alessandromaci/banb

**Live URL of your project**

https://banb.finance

**What is your product’s unique value proposition?**

BANB stands out by merging neobank simplicity with onchain intelligence. It's a a product that feels as smooth as Revolut but runs entirely on Web3 rails.
It’s not another wallet or dApp. It's a consumer app. It’s the AI-powered interface for stablecoins.

Key Differentiators

- Neobank UX, onchain
BANB delivers a familiar and elegant experience inspired by modern fintech apps with balance view, cards, and smart actions all powered by your connected wallets.

- Stable-first architecture
Built around USDC on Base, BANB ensures stable value, low fees, and predictable user flows for payments, investing, and gas. In the medium term, we plan expanding it to more stable tokens and chains.

- Multi-wallet account model
Users can link multiple wallets (via Privy or native connectors) and manage them as unified “accounts” like having multiple sub-accounts in a digital bank.

- AI-guided actions
Natural-language operations such as “Send 20 USDC to John” or “Where should I invest my idle balance?” make onchain finance conversational, not complicated.
The AI explains every recommendation, yields, risks, and trade-offs, to build trust, not hype.

- Fully non-custodial
BANB never holds your assets. All transactions happen directly through your wallets, keeping users in complete control.

Why it matters?

The alpha version shows that users can on-ramp, transact, and invest in DeFi with the same ease as a neobank, while staying self-custodial and transparent.

BANB turns stablecoin management into something intuitive: one interface, one AI, all your wallets.

**Who is your target customer?**

BANB targets Millennials and Gen Z, the same demographic driving adoption of both neo-banks (Revolut, N26) and crypto wallets.

These users:

- Value instant, mobile-first finance.
- Are comfortable using stablecoins and DeFi protocols.
- Want better returns than traditional savings accounts (0–1% in EU).

Our validation came from:

- The massive traction of Revolut and N26 across Europe.
- Market data showing that crypto adoption is highest among 18–35-year-olds.

**Who are your closest competitors and how are you different?**

Closest competitors:

Revolut (https://www.revolut.com/) / N26 (https://n26.com/) → sleek UX, but centralized and fiat-only.

Phantom (https://phantom.com/) / Trust Wallet (https://trustwallet.com/?utm_source=cryptwerk) → Web3 native, but complex UX and locked to single-chain wallets.

DolarApp (https://dolarapp.com/) → partially similar in concept, but U.S.-centric and limited in DeFi extensibility.

How BANB differs:

- Fully non-custodial (users control their funds).
- Multi-wallet, multi-chain, but unified through one dashboard.
- Stablecoin-centric, not speculative tokens.
- AI-driven experience with automated insights and actions.
- Open, modular architecture for new integrations (investments, gasless ops, identity, etc.).

**What is your distribution strategy and why?**

BANB’s go-to-market strategy focuses on Europe — where low savings rates (0–1%) and high neobank adoption create a prime market.

Tactics:

- Launch first as a Farcaster Mini App, leveraging on-chain identity and early crypto-native users.
- Run targeted paid campaigns on Instagram and TikTok showcasing stable yield and smooth UX.
- Use referral codes and reward systems to drive virality.
- Sponsor and showcase BANB at Italian ETH events (ETH Bari, ETH Milan, NapulETH).
- Over time, partner with DeFi protocols and on/off-ramp providers for embedded yield products.

The strategy ensures low CAC and high retention as every deposit, withdrawal, and investment generates protocol-level revenue that fuels further growth.

**Description of your solution**

**CirclAI** is an AI-powered Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and sustainability intelligence platform designed to revolutionize the metallurgy and mining sectors by automating environmental impact analysis and enabling a circular economy approach.

Traditional LCA tools are complex, data-sparse, and often fail to account for circularity benefits like recycling and reuse. CirclAI eliminates these limitations by using machine learning to intelligently fill data gaps, predict environmental indicators, and visualize the complete material journey—from extraction to recycling.

Through an intuitive web interface, users can input product or process data and instantly receive a comprehensive sustainability report highlighting carbon footprint, material circularity index (MCI), and energy savings potential. The platform’s AI-driven engine compares primary and secondary metal production processes, identifies inefficiencies, and provides actionable recommendations for sustainable material selection, process optimization, and cost reduction.

Built using FastAPI and PostgreSQL, CirclAI combines robust data processing with user-friendly visualization dashboards, ensuring accessibility for both industry professionals and non-experts. The system incorporates confidence scoring and human-in-the-loop validation to maintain transparency and trust in AI-generated predictions.

Beyond LCA, CirclAI helps industries transition towards net-zero manufacturing by quantifying the impact of design choices and highlighting opportunities for waste reduction, recycling, and reuse. This aligns directly with India’s sustainable development goals and the global movement toward greener supply chains.

In essence, CirclAI is not just an analytical tool—it’s a decision-support system that empowers industries to make informed, data-backed, and eco-friendly decisions, turning sustainability into a competitive advantage.

**Core Features**:

AI-Powered Data Gap Filling: Predicts missing environmental metrics with high confidence.

Circularity Insights: Calculates Material Circularity Index and identifies reuse/recycling potential.

Real-Time Visualization: Interactive dashboards showing energy savings, emissions reduction, and material flows.

Smart Recommendations: Actionable guidance for improving sustainability and reducing costs.

Accessible Design: Simplified UI for non-experts to conduct advanced LCA analysis easily.


**Tech Stack:**

Backend: FastAPI

Database: PostgreSQL

Frontend: React / Netlify

AI/ML: Python-based predictive models for LCA data estimation

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/961e52b6244b4b2ba7bf42415607093a/703b2679-9d0c-4543-8ef5-e6fc7f97d60c.jpeg)

**Misinformation: Bring your own problem in Misinformation, leveraging Agentic AI.**

In the metallurgy and mining sectors, data misinformation is a silent but serious problem. Companies often make sustainability or carbon-neutral claims based on incomplete, outdated, or biased data, leading to greenwashing and poor environmental decisions.

Our solution, CirclAI, directly tackles this misinformation challenge using Agentic AI — autonomous AI agents that can validate, correct, and enhance environmental datasets before they are used for decision-making.

Here’s how CirclAI aligns perfectly with the track:

Misinformation Detection: AI agents detect inconsistencies, missing values, or false sustainability claims in raw industrial data.

Truth Verification: The system cross-checks environmental data from trusted databases (EPA, ISO, UNEP) and flags unreliable entries.

Agentic Autonomy: AI agents autonomously fill verified gaps, explain reasoning, and generate transparent sustainability reports.

Impact Transparency: It eliminates misinformation in environmental reporting, ensuring companies base actions on accurate, explainable data.

By leveraging Agentic AI for truth verification, CirclAI transforms sustainability from a subjective narrative into a data-driven, verifiable, and misinformation-free process.
It showcases how AI agents can protect truth in data-heavy industries, aligning precisely with Mumbai Hacks’ theme of “Fighting misinformation through intelligent AI systems.”

**Description of your solution**

**Veridian** is your dedicated AI investment analyst, an intelligent platform designed to demystify real estate and empower you to invest with data-driven confidence. It moves far beyond simple property listings, acting as a tireless agent that autonomously scours, synthesizes, and analyzes vast amounts of market, legal, and geospatial data. Veridian doesn't just find you a house; it identifies high-potential assets, forecasts their future growth, audits their legal safety, and provides a clear "green light" to build your real estate portfolio.

---

### 1. Problem Understanding

Real estate in India is a cornerstone of wealth, yet for the average investor, the path is fraught with risk and complexity. The modern investor faces a flood of unstructured information and a glaring lack of sophisticated tools, leading to decisions based on gut feel rather than deep analysis.

* **Scenario 1: The Aspiring Professional.** Anjali, a software developer, is overwhelmed by hundreds of online listings. She can't differentiate true value from marketing, leading to "analysis paralysis" and inaction on her first major investment.
* **Scenario 2: The Cautious Investor.** Mr. Sharma wants a property for stable rental income but fears hidden legal disputes or developer issues, lacking the tools to verify a property's safety before committing his life savings.

---

### 2. Our Solution: Veridian

Veridian is the definitive solution, providing institutional-grade analysis in an intuitive platform. It transforms data into actionable intelligence through its core features:

1.  **AI Investment Score:** A proprietary algorithm synthesizes all data points into a single, unified **Investment Score (1-10)**, providing an immediate, objective rating of a property's potential.

2.  **Infrastructure & Proximity Analysis:** Builds a "Location DNA" by analyzing proximity to critical infrastructure (IT parks, **under-construction** metro lines, schools, etc.), translating location into a clear growth score.

3.  **Predictive Financial Modeling:** Analyzes municipal plans and news to forecast **5-year appreciation, annual rental yield, and net monthly cash flow**, providing a clear picture of your potential ROI.

4.  **Automated Legal & Risk Audit:** Acts as a preliminary legal scout, scanning public **RERA and land record databases** to flag compliance issues, developer history, and potential title disputes.

5.  **Personalized Financial Strategy:** Advises on *how* to buy. Users input their finances, and the agent recommends an optimal payment plan (loan vs. cash) to maximize tax benefits and liquidity.

6.  **Interactive Map Visualization:** Presents top-rated properties as color-coded pins on an interactive map, allowing users to visually understand the geographic context of their investments.

7.  **Automated Investment Memo:** Generates a concise summary explaining the *why* behind the score, detailing positives, risks, and a final "Verdict" in plain English.

**Addressing the Scenarios:**
* **For Anjali:** Veridian cuts through the noise. It shortlists the top 3 properties and its memo clearly explains that the property near the metro has a higher appreciation forecast, giving her the data-driven confidence to act.
* **For Mr. Sharma:** Veridian’s legal audit acts as a crucial first-pass check. It flags a developer's history of project delays from RERA data, steering him towards a safer, more reliable investment.

---

### 3. Data Sources

Veridian's intelligence is fueled by a comprehensive set of data sources:
* **Property Portals:** MagicBricks, 99acres, Housing.com, etc. (for real-time listings, pricing data).
* **Geospatial APIs:** Google Maps, OpenStreetMap (for location context and proximity analysis).
* **Government Records:** RERA portals (for developer compliance), municipal websites (for development plans), and land record databases.
* **Market Data:** News APIs and financial publications (for economic trends).

---

### 4. Technical Approach

Our platform is built on a modern, scalable, and AI-native tech stack:
* **Backend/AI:** Python with FastAPI, using the LangChain framework to power our intelligent agent.
* **Database:** PostgreSQL with PostGIS for advanced geospatial queries.
* **Frontend:** React.js with Mapbox for a dynamic, map-based UI.
* **Deployment:** The entire application is containerized with Docker for reliability and scalability.

---

### 5. Feasibility & Impact

**Feasibility**: We will go with a city-by-city rollout. Our architecture is designed to master one market's data complexities first, creating a proven and replicable playbook that ensures stable, predictable scaling to new geographies.

**Impact**: Veridian democratizes real estate investing. By providing access to sophisticated analysis once reserved for large firms, it saves users hundreds of hours of research, minimizes financial risk, and empowers them to build wealth confidently, fostering a more transparent market for everyone.

**Fintech: Bring your own problem in Fintech, leveraging Agentic AI.**

### How Veridian Aligns with the Track

Veridian is a quintessential example of the innovation this track seeks to inspire, aligning perfectly with all three of its core components:

**1. A Core Fintech Solution:**
At its heart, Veridian is a financial technology platform. While it operates in the property sector (PropTech), its primary function is to facilitate one of the most significant financial decisions an individual can make: a real estate investment. Our platform moves beyond simple listings to provide sophisticated financial modeling, including ROI projections, rental yield calculations, capital appreciation forecasts, and personalized loan strategy analysis. It is a tool for asset valuation, risk assessment, and personal wealth management, placing it firmly within the Fintech domain.

**2. Bringing a Critical, Self-Identified Problem:**
The problem we are solving is the deep **information and analysis asymmetry** that exists between institutional and retail investors in the real estate market. Today, individual investors are either drowned in unstructured data or forced to rely on gut feelings, exposing them to immense financial risk. They lack the tools for the rigorous due diligence that large firms consider standard. Veridian directly addresses this gap by democratizing access to institutional-grade, data-driven investment analysis, making the market safer and more accessible for everyone.

**3. Leveraging True Agentic AI:**
Veridian is not just a script or a dashboard; it is powered by a genuine **AI Agent**. When a user provides a goal (e.g., "find a high-growth 2BHK in Pune"), the agent doesn't follow a rigid set of instructions. Instead, it autonomously plans and executes a complex research strategy, much like a human analyst. It dynamically decides which "tools" to use—be it scraping property portals, querying geospatial databases, scanning legal records, or analyzing news—and synthesizes the findings into a coherent investment memo. This ability to reason, strategize, and orchestrate multiple tools to achieve a complex financial goal is the very definition of Agentic AI, making Veridian a forward-thinking application of this cutting-edge technology.

In essence, **Veridian** is a direct answer to this track's call for innovation. We identified a crucial problem in the personal finance space—the high-stakes gamble of real estate investing—and purpose-built a true Agentic AI to solve it. Our project isn't just a novel application of AI; it's a forward-looking **Fintech platform** where an autonomous agent delivers the clarity and confidence needed to build wealth, perfectly embodying the spirit and technical challenge of this theme.

**Description of your solution**

**Project: Arogya-Saarthi (The Health Charioteer)**
*An Agentic AI Ecosystem for Proactive Surge Control*

The Core Concept: From Insight to Action
Hospitals today don’t have a data problem; they have an action problem. They drown in passive dashboards and alerts but lack the automated response capabilities to handle predictable surges from festivals, pollution, or epidemics. **Arogya-Saarthi** solves this. It's not another analytics tool. It's an agentic AI ecosystem that functions as a hospital's central nervous system. It ingests diverse, real-time data to predict a surge 24-48 hours in advance, and critically it autonomously orchestrates a 360-degree operational response.

The Agentic Workflow: Predict, Coordinate, Act
Our system operates in a simple but powerful three-stage loop:

1. PREDICT: The Forecast Agent This agent is the "brain." It fuses external data (AQI, news-driven viral_score, weather, festival flags) with internal hospital data (bed occupancy, real-time ICU_stress_index) to generate two key outputs: admissions_next_day (the number) and surge_flag (the trigger). This isn't a simple guess; it's a high-fidelity, multi-modal forecast.

2. COORDINATE: The Coordinator Agent This is the "conductor." When the Forecast Agent triggers a surge_flag, the Coordinator doesn't just email a warning. It instantly assesses the type of surge (e.g., "High Respiratory Load") and dispatches specific, tool-equipped agents to execute a pre-defined playbook.

3. ACT: The Specialist Agents (The "Hands") This is our key differentiator. The Coordinator activates a team of specialist agents that use tools to take real-world action before the surge hits:

- Inventory Agent: Checks the internal stock database. Sees a "Respiratory Surge" is coming and stock of nebulizers is at 40%. It autonomously places a high-priority order with the pre-approved supplier via their API.

- Staffing Agent: Accesses the HR database. It sees the predicted 200 admissions require 3 on-call pulmonologists and 5 extra nurses. It drafts a new shift plan and pushes it to the Head Nurse's dashboard for one-click approval.

- Patient Communications Agent: Manages the "demand" side. It auto-drafts and pushes advisories to the hospital's app and website: "High wait times expected. For non-emergencies, please use our Telehealth service."


Why This Wins: A Closed-Loop Solution
Arogya-Saarthi is a complete, closed-loop system. It bridges the critical gap between a prediction and preparedness. While other solutions provide a "check engine light," we are providing the automated mechanic. We are turning data into decisions and decisions into actions, moving the hospital from a state of reactive chaos to proactive, automated control.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b8f0bb4bec514e6d953ec6ac5903d160/b99bbdfa-1762-4b72-b701-ffedfdf2987e.png)

**Healthtech: Manage unpredictable surges in patients during festivals, pollution spikes, or epidemics with an AI agent that autonomously analyzes data and recommends staffing, supply, and patient advisory actions in advance.**

Our project, Arogya-Saarthi, is a direct and complete solution for this exact track.

It's an agentic AI system designed specifically to manage unpredictable surges from pollution, epidemics, and festivals. It autonomously analyzes a mix of real-time data (AQI, news, internal ICU_stress_index) to forecast a surge.

Based on this forecast, it then dispatches a team of specialist agents to recommend... actions:

- An Inventory Agent manages supply by auto-ordering critical items.

- A Staffing Agent recommends optimal staffing shift plans.

- A Communications Agent drafts and sends proactive patient advisories.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b8f0bb4bec514e6d953ec6ac5903d160/3a960058-a6db-421b-a87f-e6674e933928.png)

**The problem it solves**

Exploring the solar system and understanding planetary science is often limited to static images, complex data, or text-heavy sources that fail to inspire curiosity.
People, especially students and space enthusiasts face these challenges:

🌍 Lack of Real-Time Context: Existing space websites and textbooks rarely show live or dynamic planetary conditions.

📊 Data Overload, No Experience: NASA’s open data is vast but not visually accessible or interactive for learners.

🧠 Limited Engagement: Space education can feel abstract without immersive visualization or hands-on interaction.

🗣️ No Personalized Learning Companion: There’s no AI guide that explains cosmic phenomena conversationally and contextually.

💡 How Echoes of the Solar System Solves This

🌌 Brings the Cosmos to Life: Real-time 3D visualization of the solar system using NASA and environmental APIs.

🤖 AI Space Guide “Cosmo”: Makes learning interactive. Users can chat, ask questions, and receive simplified, fun explanations about planets and stars.

🔭 Data Made Beautiful: Transforms complex scientific data into glowing “planet mood rings” that reflect temperature, atmosphere, and energy.

🌱 Promotes Awareness: By comparing Earth’s live data with other planets, users realize how rare and fragile our home world truly is.

🧭 Educational + Experiential: Perfect for classrooms, museums, and personal exploration turning learning into an adventure.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Echoes of the Solar System was a thrilling yet technically demanding journey. Some key challenges we faced:

🪐 Integrating Real-Time 3D Orbits:
Getting planets to orbit smoothly and realistically in Three.js without breaking frame rates was tough. The scaling between planet sizes and orbital distances required deep mathematical tuning.

✅ Solution: We optimized rendering with @react-three/fiber and used simplified orbital physics equations for smoother motion.

🔗 Merging Multiple APIs Seamlessly:
Combining live data from NASA, OpenWeatherMap, and AQICN caused conflicts due to rate limits and inconsistent formats.

✅ Solution: We created a Node.js middleware to normalize and cache API responses, reducing API load and improving performance.

🤖 Training the AI Chatbot “Cosmo”:
Making Cosmo stay focused only on space topics was challenging. The AI sometimes drifted into unrelated answers.

✅ Solution: We refined the system prompt to include strong content boundaries like “Answer only about astronomy, planets, or the solar system” and sanitized user input before sending it to the API.

🎨 Balancing Aesthetic & Performance:
Realistic lighting, shadows, and glow effects slowed the rendering of planets on lower-end devices.

✅ Solution: We used baked textures and adaptive quality rendering to maintain beauty without performance drops.

🌍 Representing Real-Time Earth Data:
Live environmental data often updated at irregular intervals, causing visual “jumps” in the UI.

✅ Solution: We implemented data smoothing and interpolation to make the transitions feel more natural.

**The problem it solves**

Forest Fire cause immense environmental economic and social damage and traditional detection methods are often too late to stop rapid spread. A forest fire prediction and simulation system shifts the approach from reactive to proactive by forecasting high risk areas, simulating fire behaviour and guiding emergency planning. This makes it easier anticipate outbreaks, allocate fire fighting resources, plan evacuation, and protect communities, widlife and infrastructure. By enabling early warning, risk reduction and smarter preparedness, it ultimately enhance safety and reduces the enormous costs of uncontrolled wildfires.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a forest fire prediction and simulation system wasn't without obstacles. Finding reliable datasets on weather, vegetation and past fires was tough, and modeling fire spread meant juggling many variables like wind, humidity, and terrain. Running simulations in real time also pushed performance limit, while integrating predictions with a clear, usable interface proved tricky. Finally, validating results against real fires was challenging since no two events behaves the same. Each hurdle, though, became a chance to improve the system and make it more practical

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pluto-ai-fd9e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/janeshkrish/Pluto-AI-v1.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/9Wvs6jA6IGU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-TIC%20Pinnacle%20Hacks%20--%20Edition%201-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://tic-pinnacle-hacks-2025.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI-Based Speech Command Recognition System

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![PyAudio](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyAudio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ollama](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ollama-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Speech Recognition API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Speech%20Recognition%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

A smart AI-based voice command system designed to recognize and process commands in multiple Indian languages and dialects, working fully offline.
 It enables differently-abled individuals to control computers, applications using natural voice commands in real time.

How It Addresses the Problem:
Removes the need for keyboard or mouse → Ideal for visually-impaired and mobility-challenged users.
Supports local languages and dialects → Enables use by rural and tribal communities.
Works offline for reliable performance without internet dependency.
Automates system tasks (open apps, shutdown, take screenshots) easily through simple voice commands.

**Challenges we ran into**

🎤 Speech Recognition Accuracy Crisis
Problem: Initially used complex Whisper multi-pass processing that caused:

False recognitions like hearing "Don't worry, I think I'm about to bother you" instead of "open chrome"
Division by zero errors in confidence calculations
Tamil commands like "notepad open pannu" not recognized at all

Solution:

Simplified to Google Speech Recognition for better English accuracy
Added intelligent fallback patterns for common commands
Implemented fuzzy wake word matching to handle speech recognition errors
Created hybrid Tamil detection using keyword patterns

🤖 AI Model Timeout & Failure Handling
Problem: AI models (Phi3, Llama3, Mistral) frequently timed out or failed silently, causing:
Chat queries returning empty responses
System hanging on complex requests
No user feedback when models failed

Solution:

Implemented cascading model fallbacks with different timeout strategies
Added graceful degradation with predefined responses for common queries
Created intelligent model selection based on query complexity

🔊 Real-time Audio Processing Optimization
Problem: Audio processing caused system lag and recognition delays:
VAD filter too aggressive, removing actual speech
Energy threshold miscalibration causing false triggers
Background noise interfering with wake word detection

Solution:

Tuned VAD parameters to be less aggressive with speech filtering
Implemented dynamic energy threshold adjustment based on environment
Added wake word fuzzy matching to handle recognition variations

Our **Real-Time Music Recommendation Engine** helps users:

**Challenges we ran into**

**UI Responsiveness:** Streamlit UI sometimes lagged when loading large CSVs.
👉 Fix: Pre-processed data and cached results using @st.cache in Streamlit.

**Deployment Issues:** Some dependency mismatches on Streamlit Cloud.
👉 Fix: Cleaned up requirements.txt and pinned stable library versions.

With FAQs, awareness programs, and recycling insights, WMS makes waste management simple, safe, and efficient—leading to cleaner surroundings, reduced health risks, and sustainable living.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was integrating the complaint submission system with real-time preview. Initially, data wasn’t displaying correctly due to backend–frontend mismatches. We solved it by debugging API calls, standardizing JSON formats, and ensuring proper synchronization between database and UI.

**The problem it solves**

ChatGPT said:

The Smart Bin Monitoring System is an IoT and web-based platform designed for municipalities to manage waste collection efficiently. It connects smart bins with a MERN stack dashboard using Blynk to provide real-time monitoring, driver assignment, and route management.

What people can use it for:

Municipalities can monitor all dustbins across the city in real time, get alerts when bins are full, and assign nearby drivers quickly.

Drivers can check which bins are full, get assigned bins directly, and avoid wasting trips to half-empty bins.

Citizens benefit from cleaner neighborhoods and reduced health risks from overflowing garbage.

How it makes tasks easier and safer:

Smart bins send fill level data automatically so there is no need for manual checking.

Each bin is shown on the map with a clear status: green for safe, yellow for nearly full, and red for overflowing.

Admins can assign drivers directly from the dashboard and drivers get instant updates.

Routes can be planned to save fuel and reduce collection time.

Overflowing bins are avoided, making cities cleaner and healthier.

Why this project is useful:
Traditional waste collection happens on fixed schedules, which often means half-empty bins are cleared or overflowing bins are missed. This project makes the process data-driven, reducing costs for municipalities, effort for drivers, and improving cleanliness for citizens.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was connecting the IoT bins with the web dashboard. The bins were sending sensor data to the Blynk cloud, but making that data flow into the MERN backend in real time was tricky. At first, I faced issues with webhook setup because the backend was running on localhost and Blynk required a public URL.

Another hurdle was dependency conflicts in the frontend. Packages like react-leaflet and recharts had version mismatches with React 18, which caused build failures. This slowed down development until I fixed the versions and reinstalled with legacy peer dependencies.

I also struggled with authentication and role-based access. Setting up JWT authentication with roles for staff, admin, and drivers required careful planning to ensure correct permissions and routes.

To solve these problems, I used ngrok/localtunnel to expose my backend for webhook testing, locked down package versions in package.json to prevent conflicts, and modularized authentication logic for cleaner role handling. Each step helped me stabilize the system and make it reliable for demo.
